subject: Qualification recap and prompt intake for model-fit evaluation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@acme-retail.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Aug 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & prompt intake for model-fit evaluation

Hi Morgan / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a targeted eval for model fit: 

- Goal: produce a shortlist of model+config that meets Acme's ticket triage accuracy target (~>85% correct intent classification + sensible recommendation text), with latency budget <= 350ms p50 on your inferred 2,048-token distribution.
- Deliverables: (1) short model benchmark report with token-level cost estimates, (2) a prompt set eval using your customer examples + edge cases, (3) redaction/PII guidance and a recommended ingestion pipeline for eval data.

What we need from you to kick off the eval:
1) A sample of ~150-300 representative prompts (user messages) across channels (web chat, email, returns hotline). Prefer CSV or newline-delimited; include a column for "channel" and an optional flag for "sensitive".
2) A short list of explicit edge cases we should prioritize (examples where the current classifier fails, e.g., mixed-intent messages, long quoted history, embedded order IDs).
3) Any legal/redaction constraints (PHI/PCI overlap, retention limits) and the contact we should use for compliance questions.

Initial model suggestions (based on today's product profile):
- Mistral-7B-instruct (int8/quant) — good latency/cost tradeoff for high throughput.
- Redmond-13B-fp16 — if you prioritize answer quality and can accept higher unit cost.
- Local distilled 3B variant for strict latency/embedded cases (we can benchmark fallback policies).

We can host the eval in your VPC (Private) or run it on Redwood Hosted — either way we support the same observability surface. Next step from our side: once you upload the sample prompts (or attach them to this thread), we’ll run a small smoke benchmark and share a prioritized action plan within 48 hours.

Attachment: "sample-prompts-template.csv" (template only)

Thanks — small asks up front will speed up the model-fit results.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciated. Alex and I pulled together a first batch and attached sample-prompts.csv to this reply. A few notes: 

- The attached CSV contains ~120 raw examples from live chat and our returns email inbox. We flagged ~22 rows as "sensitive" where the content contains order numbers or billing details.
- Examples of edge-cases inline: 
  * Long quoted threads where the most recent user ask is buried under previous emails.
  * Messages with mixed intent: e.g., "I want a refund but also I need a replacement ASAP".
  * User-provided structured IDs: order IDs (ORD-9843-22), SKU codes, and partial SSN-like sequences in legacy forms.

Questions from our security/legal team: will Redwood store the raw prompts used in the eval? If so, for how long and can we request deletion after the benchmark? Also, we need guidance on what to redact vs. pseudonymize — e.g., should we hash order IDs or replace them with placeholders?

We can add more edge cases once we see the first-pass feedback. Also, we have an internal compliance reviewer (Lena Park) who should be looped in if you need to clarify retention/PII handling.

--Morgan
Morgan Lee
Lead Product Manager, Conversational Experiences
Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & prompt intake for model-fit evaluation

Thanks for the CSV, Morgan — helpful slice. Quick technical guidance and proposed plan from our eval team: 

1) Storage & retention: Redwood will store the prompts temporarily for the duration of the eval run. Typical retention policy for benchmarking is 30 days by default; we can set a shorter window (7 days) for your account and confirm deletion once the report is finalized. We'll add a formal entry to the SOW/DAA if you want that guaranteed. (HubSpot: ACME-47; internal ticket NR-1234).

2) Redaction recommendations (practical):
  - Replace order IDs and numeric identifiers with stable placeholders (e.g., "<ORDER_ID>") for deterministic analysis.
  - For billing/PII-like tokens (card numbers, SSN fragments), remove or hash using HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-provided salt (this preserves similarity clustering without exposing raw values).
  - Keep channel/context and quoted history intact, but mark quoted segments with a metadata flag so the eval can ignore that earlier context when measuring intent accuracy.

3) Edge-case triggers to capture (please confirm): 
  - "Mixed intent" (refund + replacement)
  - "Implicit intent" (complaint that implies shipping delay)
  - "Embedded JSON or code" in messages (rare but confuses parsers)
  - "Long history + short last line" (quoted threads)

4) Model shortlist & quick experiments we'll run: 
  - Mistral-7B-instruct (int8) — baseline for throughput/cost.
  - Redmond-13B-fp16 — quality-focused check (A/B with Mistral).
  - Redwood-distil-3B — micro-latency/fallback for mobile.

5) Timeline (proposed):
  - Today: confirm redaction approach and retention window.
  - +48 hours after cleaned upload: smoke benchmark and short report.
  - +5 business days: full eval with prioritized failure modes and rollout recommendations (canary + cache policy).

Action items for Acme: confirm retention (we can set 7 days) and provide one more set of ~30 high-priority edge cases (copy/paste or CSV column "edge_case = true").

I've attached a draft of our redaction guidelines for your compliance review (redaction-guidelines-draft.md). Also linking a quick benchmark run example for reference: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/NR-1234.
